Language review 1 › Conditional sentence.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)

questions.q: Which is the correct form of the second conditional (Type 2)?
options: If + past simple, would + infinitive
If + present simple, will + infinitive
If + past perfect, would have + past participle
If + present simple, would + infinitive
questions.topic: Form of the second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson gives the pattern: If + past simple, would + infinitive.

questions.q: When do we use the second conditional?
options: When the condition is unlikely or impossible, so the result is unlikely too
When the condition is always true, like a fact in science
When the condition really happens at the moment of speaking
When the condition happened in the past and is now finished
questions.topic: Use of the second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson says: when a condition is not likely or impossible, the result is not likely to happen.

questions.q: Complete: *If Salem ____ the manager, he would change the work system.*
options: were
is
will be
am
questions.topic: Were with all pronouns
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: With the verb be in Type 2 we use were with all pronouns, especially in formal writing.

questions.q: In the sentence *If I knew his phone number, I would call him.*, the verb 'knew' is past simple. What does the whole sentence mean?
options: An imaginary situation about the present or the future
A real situation that happened in the past
A habit that was repeated again and again in the past
Something that will certainly happen tomorrow morning
questions.topic: Past form with present meaning in if-clauses
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson notes that the verb in the If-clause is past, but the meaning is about the present or future and is imaginary.

questions.q: Complete: *If I had more free time, I ____ join the school football team.*
options: could
will
can
would have
questions.topic: Could instead of would
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson says could or might can be used instead of would in the result clause.

questions.q: Complete: *If Nadia ____ a smartphone, she couldn't send photos to her cousin.*
options: didn't have
doesn't have
hadn't had
isn't having
questions.topic: Negative form of the second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The negative If-clause in Type 2 uses the past simple negative: If + didn't + infinitive.

questions.q: What does the sentence *If I were you, I would see a doctor about that cough.* express?
options: Advice to another person
A real event that happened last week
A scientific fact that is always true
A promise about the future
questions.topic: If I were you for advice
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson says If I were you, I would ... is used to give advice.

questions.q: Re-order these words to make a correct second-conditional sentence: *a bike / I / if / had / would / I / ride / it / to school*
options: If I had a bike, I would ride it to school.
If I would have a bike, I rode it to school.
If I have a bike, I would ride it to school.
If I had a bike, I will ride it to school.
questions.topic: Word order in the second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The If-clause takes the past simple (had) and the result clause takes would + infinitive (would ride).

questions.q: Rewrite as a second conditional: *We don't have a garden, so we don't grow vegetables.*
options: If we had a garden, we would grow vegetables.
If we have a garden, we will grow vegetables.
If we had a garden, we would have grown vegetables.
If we would have a garden, we grew vegetables.
questions.topic: Changing a real situation into a second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The real present situation becomes an unreal past form (had) plus would + infinitive.

questions.q: Rewrite with the same meaning, using 'might': *Maybe we will visit Taiz next month, but we don't have enough time.*
options: If we had enough time, we might visit Taiz next month.
If we have enough time, we might visit Taiz next month.
If we had had enough time, we might have visited Taiz next month.
If we would have enough time, we might visit Taiz next month.
questions.topic: Might in the second conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: Might can replace would in Type 2, so the If-clause takes the past simple had.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *If Sara ____ (have) a laptop, she would do her homework online.*
options: had
has
have
would have
questions.topic: Past simple after 'if' in Type 2 (have → had)
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: In Type 2 the verb after 'if' is in the past simple, so 'have' becomes 'had'; 'would' stays in the result only.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form: *If we had a bigger house, we would ____ all our cousins to stay with us.* (invite)
options: invite
invited
inviting
to invite
questions.topic: Bare infinitive after 'would'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: After 'would' we use the infinitive without 'to' — the lesson corrects 'I would flew' to 'I would fly'.

questions.q: Which sentence is the better formal English? *If I was you, I would ask the teacher. / If I were you, I would ask the teacher.*
options: The second, because 'were' is preferred with 'I' in formal English.
The first, because 'was' is the past form of 'be' with 'I'.
Both of them are correct in formal writing.
Neither of them is correct in formal writing.
questions.topic: 'If I were you' — 'were' not 'was'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson marks 'If I was you' as wrong in formal writing and prefers 'If I were you'.

questions.q: Study these two sentences: *If I finish my homework, I will go out. / If I finished my homework, I would go out.* Which statement is correct?
options: The first describes a real possibility; the second describes an imaginary or unlikely one.
The first describes an imaginary situation; the second describes a real possibility.
Both sentences describe a real possibility in the future.
Both sentences describe something that is impossible.
questions.topic: Type 1 (possible) vs Type 2 (imaginary)
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson: Type 1 means there is a real chance, while Type 2 means the situation is imaginary — 'not true now'.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *If I would have a helicopter, I would fly to Socotra.*
options: Because we must not use 'would' in the if-clause.
Because 'fly' should be 'flying' after 'would'.
Because the result should use 'will' instead of 'would'.
Because 'have' should be 'having' after 'would'.
questions.topic: No 'would' in the if-clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The lesson's rule: never put 'would' after 'if' — the correct form is 'If I had a helicopter'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *If I won a lot of money, I ____ travel around the world.*
options: would
will
would have
am going to
questions.topic: 'would' in the result clause of Type 2
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: With a past simple if-clause (won), the result takes 'would + infinitive', not 'will'.

questions.q: Find the sentence that contains a mistake: *If we had a garden, we would grow vegetables. / If my father had more free time, he would read more books. / If she studies hard, she would pass the exam. / They would play football if they had a bigger playground.*
options: If she studies hard, she would pass the exam.
If we had a garden, we would grow vegetables.
If my father had more free time, he would read more books.
They would play football if they had a bigger playground.
questions.topic: Mixing a present if-clause with 'would'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: A present simple if-clause (studies) must go with 'will', not 'would' — 'If she studied hard, she would pass'.

questions.q: Rewrite this real situation as a second conditional: *We do not live by the sea, so we do not swim every day.*
options: If we lived by the sea, we would swim every day.
If we live by the sea, we will swim every day.
If we had lived by the sea, we would swim every day.
If we would live by the sea, we would swim every day.
questions.topic: Turning a real situation into a Type 2 conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: The real situation is turned into an imaginary one: past simple after 'if' + 'would + infinitive' in the result.

questions.q: Change this first conditional into a second conditional: *If he studies medicine, he will become a doctor.*
options: If he studied medicine, he would become a doctor.
If he studies medicine, he would become a doctor.
If he had studied medicine, he would become a doctor.
If he would study medicine, he would become a doctor.
questions.topic: Changing a Type 1 sentence into Type 2
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الثاني Type 2 (شرط غير محتمل أو مستحيل)
questions.why: Both parts change: the present simple becomes past simple after 'if', and 'will' becomes 'would'.

Language review 1 › Conditional sentence.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)

questions.q: A conditional sentence has two parts. What is the part that begins with "If" called?
options: the if clause
the main clause
the noun clause
the verb clause
questions.topic: The two parts of a conditional sentence: the if clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The if clause is the part that begins with If; the other part is the main clause, which gives the result.

questions.q: Complete the rule with the correct words: *If + ____ , will + infinitive.*
options: present simple
past simple
present continuous
will + infinitive
questions.topic: Type 1 form: if + present simple, will + infinitive
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The lesson gives the form of Type 1 as: If + present simple, will + infinitive.

questions.q: When do we use a Type 1 conditional sentence?
options: When the condition is likely to happen and the result is expected
When the condition is imagined and can never happen
When we want to talk about a past habit
When we want to ask someone to do something
questions.topic: Use of Type 1: a likely condition, a likely result
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The book says: when a condition is likely to be fulfilled, the result is likely to happen.

questions.q: Complete: *If he ____ his homework before dinner, he will go to the match.*
options: finishes
will finish
finish
finished
questions.topic: Adding -s with he / she / it in the if clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: With he/she/it we add -s to the verb in the if clause, and we do not use will there.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *If she will bring her laptop, we will finish the project today.*
options: "Will" must not be used in the if clause; the present simple is used there
"Will" can only be used in questions
The if clause must always come after the main clause
Both clauses must use "would" instead of "will"
questions.topic: No 'will' in the if clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: In the if clause we use the present simple even when the meaning is future: If she brings her laptop, we will finish.

questions.q: Join the two parts to make one correct Type 1 sentence: *we will go out / the weather is good*
options: We will go out if the weather is good.
We will go out, if the weather is good.
We will go out if the weather will be good.
We will go out if the weather good.
questions.topic: Word order and the comma before 'if'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: When the main clause comes first, If comes in the middle and we do not put a comma before it, and the if clause stays in the present simple.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form: *If she studies hard, she ____ fail the exam.*
options: won't
doesn't
isn't
didn't
questions.topic: Negative result with 'won't'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The negative of will is won't, and the negative form belongs to the main clause (the result), not to the if clause.

questions.q: In a Type 1 conditional, which words can be used in the main clause instead of "will"?
options: can / may / might / should
did / was / were / had
am / is / are / be
do / does / did / done
questions.topic: can / may / might / should instead of will
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The lesson says can, may, might or should can replace will in the main clause.

questions.q: Rewrite this sentence beginning with "If": *Unless you take an umbrella, you will get wet.*
options: If you do not take an umbrella, you will get wet.
If you take an umbrella, you will get wet.
If you do not take an umbrella, you will not get wet.
If you will not take an umbrella, you will get wet.
questions.topic: unless = if not
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: unless means if not, so Unless you take becomes If you do not take, and the result stays the same.

questions.q: Rewrite the two sentences as one Type 1 conditional sentence: *Water the plants every day. They will grow quickly.*
options: If you water the plants every day, they will grow quickly.
If you will water the plants every day, they will grow quickly.
If you watering the plants every day, they will grow quickly.
If you watered the plants every day, they will grow quickly.
questions.topic: Joining two ideas into one Type 1 sentence
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The if clause takes the present simple (water) and the main clause keeps will + infinitive (will grow).

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of the verb: *If you ____ (drink) enough water, you will feel better.*
options: drink
will drink
drank
are drinking
questions.topic: Present simple after 'if'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The if-clause takes the present simple, not 'will': If you drink enough water…

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of 'be': *If the weather ____ good tomorrow, we will have a picnic in the mountains.*
options: is
will be
was
be
questions.topic: The verb 'be' in the if-clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The if-clause keeps the present simple, so the verb 'be' becomes 'is'.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of the verb: *Our team will win the match if it ____ (practise) every evening.*
options: practises
practise
will practise
practising
questions.topic: Third person -s in the if-clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The subject 'it' takes the present simple with -s in the if-clause: if it practises.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of the verb: *The plants will die if you ____ (not / water) them every day.*
options: don't water
won't water
didn't water
aren't watering
questions.topic: Negative if-clause
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: A negative if-clause uses don't/doesn't + base verb: if you don't water them.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *If I will finish my homework, I will watch the match.*
options: If I finish my homework, I will watch the match.
If I will finish my homework, I watch the match.
If I finished my homework, I will watch the match.
If I finish my homework, I watch the match.
questions.topic: No 'will' after 'if'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: 'Will' is never used in the if-clause; it stays only in the main clause.

questions.q: Re-order the words to make a correct Type 1 sentence: *go / will / we / to the park / if / stops / the rain*
options: We will go to the park if the rain stops.
We will go to the park if the rain stop.
We go will to the park if the rain stops.
If the rain stops, will we go to the park.
questions.topic: Word order in a Type 1 sentence
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: The if-clause can come first or second, but 'will' stays in the main clause and never follows 'if'.

questions.q: Rewrite as a Type 1 conditional: *Leave now, or we will miss the train.*
options: If we don't leave now, we will miss the train.
If we don't leave now, we would miss the train.
If we leave now, we will miss the train.
If we won't leave now, we will miss the train.
questions.topic: Turning an 'or' sentence into a conditional
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: 'Leave now, or…' means the same as a negative if-clause: If we don't leave now, we will miss the train.

questions.q: Rewrite with *unless* so that the meaning stays the same: *If she doesn't apologise, I won't speak to her.*
options: Unless she apologises, I won't speak to her.
Unless she doesn't apologise, I won't speak to her.
Unless she apologises, I will speak to her.
Unless she will apologise, I won't speak to her.
questions.topic: Using 'unless' instead of 'if … not'
questions.lesson: Conditional sentences - النوع الأول Type 1 (شرط محتمل الحدوث)
questions.why: 'Unless' already carries the negative meaning, so the verb after it is affirmative: Unless she apologises…

Language review 2 › The Passive - معنى ا.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does the passive allow us to choose in a sentence?
options: What we want to make more important — the doer or the thing done
How many people did the action in the sentence
Whether the action happened in the past or in the present
Which tense of be we must use in the sentence
questions.topic: Purpose of the passive (what we make important)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The lesson says the passive allows us to choose what we want to make more important: the doer or the thing done.

questions.q: Complete the rule: The passive is formed with be (in the correct tense) + ____ of the main verb.
options: the past participle (V3)
the present participle (V-ing)
the base form (V1)
the past simple form (V2)
questions.topic: General form of the passive (be + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The general form of the passive is be in the correct tense + the past participle of the main verb.

questions.q: The lesson lists the forms of be that appear in a passive sentence. Which group contains ONLY forms of be?
options: is, are, was, were
do, does, did, done
have, has, had, having
was, were, went, gone
questions.topic: Forms of be in the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: is, are, was and were are all forms of be listed in the lesson, while the other groups contain verbs that are not be.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the verb in brackets: *The new song was ____ by a young singer.* (sing)
options: sung
sang
singing
sing
questions.topic: Main verb in the past participle
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The main verb in the passive is always the past participle, so sing becomes sung.

questions.q: Both sentences describe the same event. What is the difference between them? *A famous writer wrote this story.* / *This story was written by a famous writer.*
options: The first makes the doer important; the second makes the thing done important.
The first is in the present; the second is in the past.
The first has no subject; the second has no object.
The first is passive; the second is active.
questions.topic: Focus: active vs passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The active sentence starts with the doer, while the passive starts with the thing done, so the thing becomes the important part.

questions.q: Complete with the correct passive form: *Rice ____ in many parts of Asia every year.* (grow)
options: is grown
is growing
grows
was grown
questions.topic: Present simple passive (is + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: A general fact with every year needs be in the present + the past participle: is grown.

questions.q: Why is the phrase *by a Yemeni engineer* used in this sentence? *This bridge was designed by a Yemeni engineer.*
options: To tell us who did the action.
To tell us when the action happened.
To tell us what the bridge is made of.
To tell us where the bridge is.
questions.topic: The by-phrase naming the doer
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: After a passive verb, a by-phrase names the doer — the person or thing that did the action.

questions.q: Which sentence does NOT tell us who did the action?
options: *The letters were delivered this morning.*
*The letters were delivered by the postman.*
*The postman delivered the letters.*
*The postman has delivered the letters.*
questions.topic: Passive sentences without a by-phrase
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: Only this sentence has no by-phrase, so the doer of the action is not mentioned at all.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *The workers must repair the road before winter.*
options: The road must repaired before winter.
The road must be repaired before winter.
The road must be repair before winter.
The road is must repaired before winter.
questions.topic: Passive with a modal (must be + V3)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: With a modal the passive is modal + be + past participle: must be repaired.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *Someone has taken my keys.*
options: My keys were been taken.
My keys has been taken.
My keys have taken.
My keys have been taken.
questions.topic: Present perfect passive (have been + V3)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The present perfect passive is has/have + been + past participle, and the unknown doer (someone) is left out.

questions.q: In a passive sentence, what is the function of __by__?
options: It introduces the doer (the agent) of the action.
It introduces the receiver of the action.
It shows the tense of the main verb.
It replaces the auxiliary verb be.
questions.topic: Function of by (introducing the doer)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The lesson says we use by with the doer (or agent), so by introduces the person or thing that does the action.

questions.q: When do we add __by__ + the doer in a passive sentence?
options: When the doer is a general word such as people or they.
When the doer is important or gives new information.
When the action happened in the past.
When the object of the active sentence is plural.
questions.topic: When to mention the doer with by
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: We mention the doer after by only when it is important or new information, as in The tower was built by King William.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form: *The letters were ____ to the wrong address yesterday.* (send / sent / sending / sends)
options: send
sent
sending
sends
questions.topic: Past participle (third form) after be
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: After be we must use the third form of the verb: send → sent.

questions.q: In the passive, what do we call the person or thing that does the action?
options: The receiver of the action
The main verb of the sentence
The agent (the doer)
The object of the passive sentence
questions.topic: Meaning of the agent (the doer)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: The lesson says we use by with 'the doer (or agent)', so the doer is called the agent.

questions.q: Which of these sentences is written correctly?
options: Fresh bread is sold in that shop every morning by people.
Fresh bread is sold in that shop every morning.
Fresh bread sold in that shop every morning by someone.
Fresh bread is sold in that shop every morning by they.
questions.topic: Leaving out an unnecessary by + people phrase
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: When the doer is a general word like people, we do not mention it, so no by-phrase is needed.

questions.q: Complete: *The old bridge ____ in the flood last year.* (was destroyed / destroyed / was destroy / is destroyed)
options: destroyed
was destroy
was destroyed
is destroyed
questions.topic: Missing be in the passive (was/were + third form)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: A passive sentence must have be + the third form, and the time is past: was destroyed.

questions.q: Why is the doer not mentioned in *My wallet was taken from my bag*?
options: Because the doer is a famous person everybody knows
Because the sentence has no past participle
Because the doer is unknown
Because the wallet is the doer of the action
questions.topic: Omitting an unknown doer
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: We leave out the doer when it is unknown; the sentence tells us nothing about who took the wallet.

questions.q: Re-order the words to make a correct passive sentence: *was / my phone / repaired / yesterday*
options: My phone repaired yesterday.
My phone was repair yesterday.
My phone repaired was yesterday.
My phone was repaired yesterday.
questions.topic: Word order in the passive (object first)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: In the passive the object comes first, then be in the same tense + the third form: My phone was repaired.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *They must clean the classroom every day.*
options: The classroom must cleaned every day.
The classroom must be cleaned every day.
The classroom must be clean every day.
The classroom must been cleaned every day.
questions.topic: Passive with a modal (must be + third form)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: After a modal we use be + the third form of the verb: must be cleaned.

questions.q: Change into the passive and keep the doer: *A young engineer designed these two hotels.*
options: These two hotels was designed by a young engineer.
These two hotels were design by a young engineer.
These two hotels were designed by a young engineer.
These two hotels designed by a young engineer.
questions.topic: Plural agreement in the passive (were + third form)
questions.lesson: The Passive - معنى المبني للمجهول ومتى نذكر الفاعل (by)
questions.why: A plural object becomes a plural subject, so we use were + designed, and the important doer is kept after by.

Language review 1 › Adjective order | تر.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم

questions.q: Choose the phrase with the adjectives in the correct order: *tiny / oval / steel*
options: a tiny oval steel table
an oval tiny steel table
a steel tiny oval table
a tiny steel oval table
questions.topic: Order of adjective categories
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Size comes before shape, and shape comes before material, so the order is tiny – oval – steel.

questions.q: Which group of adjectives comes closest to the noun, last in the adjective order?
options: Material: steel, glass, stone
Opinion: delicious, terrible, ugly
Colour: grey, purple, silver
Nationality: Turkish, Japanese, Indian
questions.topic: Position of material adjectives
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson's list ends with Material, so material adjectives stand nearest the noun, after all the others.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct adjective order: *We had ____ at the new restaurant.* (delicious / Turkish)
options: a delicious Turkish meal
a Turkish delicious meal
a delicious meal Turkish
a Turkish meal delicious
questions.topic: Word order inside a noun phrase (opinion + nationality)
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Opinion (delicious) comes before nationality (Turkish) in the lesson's order.

questions.q: According to the lesson, how many adjectives do we usually use before a noun in the same sentence?
options: No more than three
No more than two
Five or six
As many as we like
questions.topic: Number of adjectives used before a noun
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson says we usually do not use more than three adjectives in the same sentence.

questions.q: In the phrase *a fantastic Egyptian film*, why does 'fantastic' come before 'Egyptian'?
options: Because opinion adjectives come before adjectives of nationality
Because nationality adjectives are fact adjectives, so they come first
Because adjectives are arranged from the longest to the shortest
Because the noun must come before the nationality adjective
questions.topic: Reason opinion adjectives come first
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The order puts Opinion first and Nationality later, so the speaker's opinion stands before the fact of nationality.

questions.q: What is the difference between English and Arabic in the position of the adjective?
options: In English the adjective comes before the noun, but in Arabic it comes after the noun.
In English the adjective comes after the noun, but in Arabic it comes before the noun.
In both languages the adjective comes before the noun.
In both languages the adjective comes after the noun.
questions.topic: Position of adjectives in English compared with Arabic
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson states that in English the adjective comes before the noun, the opposite of Arabic.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *She wore ____ to the wedding.* (Indian / silk)
options: an Indian silk scarf
a silk Indian scarf
an Indian scarf silk
a scarf Indian silk
questions.topic: Nationality before material
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Nationality (Indian) comes before material (silk) in the lesson's order.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *They showed us ____ in the city centre.* (amazing / modern)
options: an amazing modern building
a amazing modern building
an modern amazing building
a modern amazing building
questions.topic: Choosing a or an before the first adjective
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The first adjective 'amazing' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an', and opinion comes before age.

questions.q: Re-order the words to make a correct sentence: *bought / a / glass / beautiful / she / round / vase*
options: She bought a beautiful round glass vase.
She bought a round beautiful glass vase.
She bought a glass beautiful round vase.
She bought a beautiful glass round vase.
questions.topic: Building a sentence with three adjectives in the right order
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Opinion (beautiful) comes before shape (round), and shape comes before material (glass).

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *My sister has a silk long red beautiful dress.*
options: My sister has a beautiful long red silk dress.
My sister has a beautiful red long silk dress.
My sister has a silk beautiful long red dress.
My sister has a long beautiful red silk dress.
questions.topic: Correcting a sentence with the wrong adjective order
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The adjectives must be rearranged as opinion (beautiful) – size (long) – colour (red) – material (silk) before the noun.

questions.q: According to the lesson, which is the correct order of adjective groups before a noun?
options: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material
size, opinion, shape, age, material, origin, colour
material, origin, colour, shape, age, size, opinion
origin, material, age, size, opinion, colour, shape
questions.topic: Order of adjective groups before a noun
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson labels every example in this order: opinion first, then size, age, shape, colour, origin, and material last.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence so that the adjective is in the right place: *She lives in a house old near the school.*
options: She lives in an old house near the school.
She lives in old a house near the school.
She lives in a house near the school old.
She lives in old house near a school.
questions.topic: Adjective position before the noun
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: An adjective describing a noun comes before the noun, so we say an old house, not a house old.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *She bought three reds jackets for the winter.*
options: She bought three red jackets for the winter.
She bought three reds jacket for the winter.
She bought three jacket reds for the winter.
She bought red three jackets for the winter.
questions.topic: Adjectives are not pluralized
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: An English adjective never takes -s, so we say three red jackets, not three reds jackets.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the adjectives in the correct order: *Our school invited a ____ teacher to the science club.*
options: young Canadian
Canadian young
young Canada
Canada young
questions.topic: Age before nationality
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The adjective of age (young) comes before the adjective of nationality (Canadian).

questions.q: The lesson says that both *short curly black hair* and *short, black, curly hair* are used. What does this show?
options: Both orders are acceptable when the adjectives are separated by commas.
The adjective of colour always comes before the adjective of shape.
The adjective of shape always comes after the noun.
Adjectives of size must always be separated by commas.
questions.topic: Commas in adjective order with hair
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson notes that the book wrote short, black, curly hair and that both orders are used with commas.

questions.q: Which sentence has the adjectives in the wrong order?
options: They live in a lovely modern stone house.
He is a talented young Egyptian player.
She bought a leather black new bag.
We saw a tiny round metal table.
questions.topic: Order of age, colour and material
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Age, colour and material come in that order, so it should be a new black leather bag.

questions.q: Why is this phrase wrong? *a plastic new bottle*
options: Because the adjective of material comes after the adjective of age.
Because the adjective of age comes after the adjective of material.
Because adjectives of material come before the article a.
Because an adjective must come after the noun it describes.
questions.topic: Material adjective comes last
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The lesson puts the material last in the order, so the correct phrase is a new plastic bottle.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the adjective groups in the correct order: *They visited a ____ mosque in Sana'a.*
options: beautiful old white
old beautiful white
white old beautiful
old white beautiful
questions.topic: Opinion before age and colour
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: Opinion comes first, then age, then colour, so a beautiful old white mosque is correct.

questions.q: Re-order these words to make a correct sentence: *car / a / red / Japanese / new / small*
options: A small new red Japanese car.
A new small red Japanese car.
A small red new Japanese car.
A red small new Japanese car.
questions.topic: Size and age before colour and origin
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The order is size, age, colour, origin, so a small new red Japanese car is correct.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *She wore a cotton long white shirt to the party.*
options: She wore a long white cotton shirt to the party.
She wore a long cotton white shirt to the party.
She wore a white long cotton shirt to the party.
She wore a cotton white long shirt to the party.
questions.topic: Material after size and colour
questions.lesson: Adjective order | ترتيب الصفات قبل الاسم
questions.why: The material adjective comes last, after size and colour, so a long white cotton shirt is correct.

Language review 1 › Talking about the pa.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر

questions.q: When do we use the Past simple tense?
options: For the general past and for definite times in the past
For an action that continued for some time in the past
For an action that is still happening at the moment of speaking
For an action that will be finished at a time in the future
questions.topic: Use of the Past simple
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The lesson says the Past simple is used for the general past and for definite times in the past.

questions.q: Which is the correct form of the Past continuous tense?
options: was / were + verb + ing
did + verb in the base form
have / has + past participle
was / were + past participle
questions.topic: Form of the Past continuous
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The lesson gives the Past continuous form as was / were + the verb with -ing.

questions.q: Make the sentence negative: *She visited her grandmother yesterday.*
options: She didn't visit her grandmother yesterday.
She doesn't visit her grandmother yesterday.
She didn't visited her grandmother yesterday.
She wasn't visit her grandmother yesterday.
questions.topic: Negative form of the Past simple
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The Past simple negative is didn't + the base form, so 'didn't visited' and 'wasn't visit' are wrong.

questions.q: Choose the correct time expression for the Past simple: *We moved to a new house ____.* (last month / next month / now / tomorrow)
options: last month
next month
now
tomorrow
questions.topic: Time expression for a definite past time
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'Last month' points to a definite time in the past, so the Past simple 'moved' is correct.

questions.q: Read the sentence: *When the teacher came in, the students were talking.* Which action continued for some time?
options: The students' talking
The teacher's coming in
Both actions lasted the same time
Neither action lasted any time
questions.topic: Longer action vs shorter action
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'Were talking' is the longer continuing action, and 'came in' is the shorter action that happened in the middle of it.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form: *I ____ (wait) for the bus when it started to rain.*
options: was waiting
were waiting
was waited
waiting
questions.topic: was / were agreement with I
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'I' takes 'was', and the Past continuous is was / were + verb-ing, so 'was waiting' is the only correct form.

questions.q: Which word does not belong with the Past simple? *yesterday / last week / ago / next month*
options: yesterday
last week
ago
next month
questions.topic: Words that show the future, not the past
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'Next month' points to the future, while yesterday, last week and ago all point to the past.

questions.q: In the sentence *She was cooking when the phone rang*, why is the Past continuous used for 'was cooking'?
options: Because the cooking was still continuing when the shorter action happened
Because the cooking had finished before the phone rang
Because 'was' is used with every pronoun in the past
Because the phone rang more than once
questions.topic: Reason for using the Past continuous with a shorter action
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The Past continuous shows the longer action that was in progress when the shorter Past simple action interrupted it.

questions.q: Make the sentence negative, keeping it in the Past continuous: *The boys were playing in the street.*
options: The boys weren't playing in the street.
The boys wasn't playing in the street.
The boys didn't playing in the street.
The boys didn't play in the street.
questions.topic: Negative form of the Past continuous
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The negative is was / were + not + verb-ing, and 'the boys' takes 'were', so 'weren't playing' is correct.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *While we was travelling to Aden, we saw a lot of camels.*
options: While we were travelling to Aden, we saw a lot of camels.
While we was travel to Aden, we saw a lot of camels.
While we were travel to Aden, we saw a lot of camels.
While we did travelling to Aden, we saw a lot of camels.
questions.topic: Correcting was / were with we
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'We' takes 'were', so the only error is 'was', which must become 'were' before travelling.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: When the guests ____, we were having tea in the living room.
options: arrived
was arriving
arrive
have arrived
questions.topic: when + past simple
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: After 'when' the short action is in the past simple, so 'arrived' is correct.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: She ____ off the computer, closed the window and left the office.
options: switched
was switching
switches
has switched
questions.topic: consecutive actions in the past simple
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: Actions that happen one after another are all in the past simple, so 'switched' is correct.

questions.q: Read the sentence *I was watering the plants when my father called me.* Why is 'was watering' in the past continuous?
options: Because it is the longer action that was already in progress.
Because it is the short action that interrupted the longer one.
Because two long actions happened at the same time.
Because it is a habit that was repeated in the past.
questions.topic: why the longer action takes the past continuous
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'was watering' is the longer background action; the short action 'called' takes the past simple.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'when' and 'while' in this lesson?
options: 'When' takes the short action in the past simple, and 'while' takes the longer action in the past continuous.
'When' takes the longer action in the past continuous, and 'while' takes the short action in the past simple.
'When' and 'while' both take the short action in the past simple.
'When' and 'while' both take the longer action in the past continuous.
questions.topic: the difference between when and while
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The lesson gives 'when' with the short past simple action and 'while' with the longer past continuous action.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in the sentence: *The players was training hard before the match.*
options: The players were training hard before the match.
The players was training hard before the match.
The players were train hard before the match.
The players is training hard before the match.
questions.topic: was/were agreement with a plural subject
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: With a plural subject like 'the players' we use 'were', not 'was'.

questions.q: Three of these sentences describe an action that was in progress in the past. Which one does NOT?
options: He has painted the door.
She was reading a novel at midnight.
They were climbing the mountain at noon.
I was waiting for a taxi when you called.
questions.topic: recognising the past continuous
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'He has painted the door' is present perfect, not an action in progress in the past.

questions.q: Join the two sentences with 'while': *The children were playing in the garden. Their mother came home.*
options: While the children were playing in the garden, their mother came home.
While the children played in the garden, their mother came home.
While the children were playing in the garden, their mother was coming home.
While the children were playing in the garden, their mother comes home.
questions.topic: joining a background action and an interrupting action with while
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'While' joins the longer action in the past continuous to the short action in the past simple.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence as a question, keeping the same tense: *Mona was writing an email when the electricity went off.*
options: Was Mona writing an email when the electricity went off?
Did Mona was writing an email when the electricity went off?
Was Mona write an email when the electricity went off?
Did Mona write an email when the electricity went off?
questions.topic: past continuous question form with a when-clause
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي البسيط والماضي المستمر
questions.why: In a past continuous question 'was' comes before the subject and the verb stays in -ing.

Language review 2 › The Passive - المبني.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة

questions.q: Choose the correct present simple passive form: *Our city ____ by an elected council.* (govern)
options: is governed
governs
is governing
was governed
questions.topic: Present simple passive (am / is / are + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The present simple passive is am/is/are + past participle, and 'our city' is singular, so 'is governed'.

questions.q: Choose the correct past simple passive form: *The old bridge ____ in 1954.* (build)
options: was built
is built
has been built
were built
questions.topic: Past simple passive (was / were + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'In 1954' needs the past simple, and 'the old bridge' is singular, so 'was built'.

questions.q: Choose the correct present perfect passive form: *Several old roads in our town ____ since last year.* (repair)
options: have been repaired
have repaired
has been repaired
were been repaired
questions.topic: Present perfect passive (have / has + been + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The present perfect passive is have/has + been + past participle, and 'several old roads' is plural, so 'have been repaired'.

questions.q: Choose the correct form after the modal: *Every bag ____ at the airport.* (must / check)
options: must be checked
must checked
must be checking
must been checked
questions.topic: Modal + be + past participle (must / should / will / can)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: After a modal verb we use be + past participle, so 'must be checked'.

questions.q: Choose the correct pair of forms: *The hospital ____ in 1990, and since then it ____ twice.* (build / extend)
options: was built … has been extended
has been built … was extended
was built … was extended
is built … has been extended
questions.topic: Past simple passive vs present perfect passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'In 1990' takes the past simple passive, and 'since then' takes the present perfect passive.

questions.q: In the sentence *The road was repaired last week*, why is the person who repaired it not mentioned?
options: Because the doer is unknown or not important
Because the passive can never show who did the action
Because the sentence is in the active voice
Because the past simple passive cannot take a doer
questions.topic: Omitting the agent in the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The agent is left out when the doer is unknown or unimportant, which the lesson marks as 'no agent'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *The school rules must not broken.*
options: The school rules must not be broken.
The school rules must not broken.
The school rules must not been broken.
The school rules must not broke.
questions.topic: Negative passive with modals (must not be + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: After 'must not' we need be + past participle, so 'must not be broken'.

questions.q: Which of these sentences is in the passive voice?
options: The new stadium will be finished next month.
They will finish the new stadium next month.
The new stadium will finish next month.
The new stadium is finishing next month.
questions.topic: Future passive (will + be + past participle)
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'will be finished' is will + be + past participle, which is the passive form.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *The manager must sign these reports today.*
options: These reports must be signed today.
These reports must signed today.
These reports must be sign today.
These reports must been signed today.
questions.topic: Changing a modal sentence into the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The object 'these reports' becomes the subject and 'must' keeps be + past participle: 'must be signed'.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *Someone has stolen my bicycle.*
options: My bicycle has been stolen.
My bicycle has stolen.
My bicycle was been stolen.
My bicycle have been stolen.
questions.topic: Changing a present perfect sentence into the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The present perfect passive is have/has + been + past participle, and 'my bicycle' is singular, so 'has been stolen'.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct passive form of the present continuous?
options: is / are + being + past participle
is / are + past participle
was / were + being + past participle
is / are + been + past participle
questions.topic: Passive form of the present continuous
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: In the present continuous passive, 'be' takes the form 'being' and is followed by the past participle, as in 'The road is being repaired.'

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: *A new library ____ in our town next year.*
options: is going to built
is going to build
is going to be built
is going to being built
questions.topic: Passive with 'going to'
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: With 'going to' the passive needs 'be' before the past participle: is / are going to + be + pp.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: *By the time the guests arrived, all the food ____.*
options: has been eaten
had been eaten
had eaten
was eating
questions.topic: Passive of the past perfect
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The past perfect passive is had + been + past participle, and it shows an action finished before another past action.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: *The school garden must ____ every morning.*
options: be watered
watered
being watered
is watered
questions.topic: Passive after modal verbs
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: After a modal verb such as 'must' the passive is modal + be + past participle, never 'is' or '-ing'.

questions.q: Which of these sentences is NOT in the passive voice? *The manager had signed the contract. / The broken computers have been repaired. / The children were being tested by the doctor. / The shop will be closed for two days.*
options: The broken computers have been repaired.
The children were being tested by the doctor.
The manager had signed the contract.
The shop will be closed for two days.
questions.topic: Recognising passive and active sentences
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'The manager had signed the contract' is active: the doer comes before the verb and there is no be + past participle.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *The final results will announced tomorrow.*
options: Because 'will' must be followed by 'be' and the past participle.
Because 'will' cannot be used in the passive voice.
Because 'announced' should be changed to 'announcing'.
Because the sentence needs 'had' instead of 'will'.
questions.topic: Need for 'be' + past participle in the future passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: Without 'be' before the past participle there is no passive, so the correct form is 'will be announced'.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *While the new stadium ____, heavy rain stopped the work.*
options: was building
was being built
is being built
had been built
questions.topic: Past continuous passive in a time clause
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: The stadium receives the action while the work was going on, so the past continuous passive 'was being built' is needed.

questions.q: What is the difference between these two sentences? *The letters are being typed now. / The letters were being typed at noon.*
options: The first is past continuous passive and the second is present continuous passive.
The first is present perfect passive and the second is past perfect passive.
Both sentences are in the active voice.
The first is present continuous passive and the second is past continuous passive.
questions.topic: Difference between present continuous passive and past continuous passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'are being' marks the present continuous passive, while 'were being' marks the past continuous passive.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *People must wear helmets on this building site.*
options: Helmets must be worn on this building site.
Helmets must worn on this building site.
Helmets must be wearing on this building site.
Helmets must are worn on this building site.
questions.topic: Changing a sentence with 'must' into the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: With 'must' the passive is must + be + past participle, and the object 'helmets' becomes the new subject.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *The workers were cleaning the streets while we were on holiday.*
options: The streets were cleaned while we were on holiday.
The streets are being cleaned while we were on holiday.
The streets were being cleaned while we were on holiday.
The streets had been cleaned while we were on holiday.
questions.topic: Changing a past continuous sentence into the passive
questions.lesson: The Passive - المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة والأفعال الناقصة
questions.why: 'were cleaning' keeps its past continuous tense in the passive as 'were being cleaned', not 'were cleaned'.

Language review 1 › Direct and indirect.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام

questions.q: Which of these is a correct indirect question?
options: Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
Could you tell me where is the nearest pharmacy?
Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy?
Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy are?
questions.topic: Word order in indirect questions (question word + subject + verb)
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: In an indirect question the order is question word + subject + verb, so 'is' comes after 'the nearest pharmacy'.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: I wonder where my brother has gone.
I wonder where my brother has gone?
I'd like to know where my brother has gone?
Do you know where my brother has gone.
questions.topic: Punctuation: full stop after I wonder / I'd like to know
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: 'I wonder ...' is a statement and ends with a full stop, while 'Do you know ...?' ends with a question mark.

questions.q: You are at a job interview in Sana'a. Why is the indirect question *Could you tell me what the salary is?* better than the direct question *What is the salary?*
options: Because it sounds more polite in formal situations.
Because it is shorter and quicker to say.
Because direct questions are never used in English.
Because it can only be used with close friends.
questions.topic: Politeness: when to use indirect questions
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: The lesson says we use indirect questions to be more polite, especially with strangers and in formal situations such as interviews.

questions.q: Which of these sentences is a direct question?
options: Where does your father work?
Do you know where your father works?
Could you tell me where your father works?
I'd like to know where your father works.
questions.topic: Direct and indirect question forms
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: A direct question has question word + auxiliary + subject and a question mark, but the other three begin with an introductory phrase.

questions.q: Change the direct question *How can I get to the airport?* into an indirect question beginning with 'Could you tell me ...'.
options: Could you tell me how I can get to the airport?
Could you tell me how can I get to the airport?
Could you tell me how do I can get to the airport?
Could you tell me how I can to get to the airport?
questions.topic: Position of the auxiliary can / is / will after the subject
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: The auxiliary 'can' moves after the subject: question word + subject (I) + can + main verb.

questions.q: Change the question *How often does your sister visit the doctor?* into an indirect question beginning with 'Do you know ...'.
options: Do you know how often your sister visits the doctor?
Do you know how often does your sister visit the doctor?
Do you know how often your sister visit the doctor?
Do you know how often your sister visited the doctor?
questions.topic: Changing does into verb + s in an indirect question
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: We drop 'does' and add -s to the main verb, so 'does ... visit' becomes 'visits'.

questions.q: Change the question *When did the team arrive in Aden?* into an indirect question beginning with 'Can you tell me ...'.
options: Can you tell me when the team arrived in Aden?
Can you tell me when did the team arrive in Aden?
Can you tell me when the team arrive in Aden?
Can you tell me when the team arrives in Aden?
questions.topic: Changing did into the past simple in an indirect question
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: We drop 'did' and put the main verb in the past: 'arrive' becomes 'arrived'.

questions.q: Make an indirect question from *Is the library open on Friday?* Begin with 'Do you know ...'.
options: Do you know if the library is open on Friday?
Do you know if is the library open on Friday?
Do you know when the library is open on Friday?
Do you know does the library open on Friday?
questions.topic: Using if / whether with yes-no questions
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: There is no question word in this question, so we use 'if' (or 'whether') and keep normal word order.

questions.q: This change needs two steps. Turn *Does your father work in a hospital?* into an indirect question beginning with 'Could you tell me ...'.
options: Could you tell me if your father works in a hospital?
Could you tell me if does your father work in a hospital?
Could you tell me if your father work in a hospital?
Could you tell me does your father work in a hospital?
questions.topic: Two-step change: adding if and changing does to verb + s
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: Step 1: add 'if' because there is no question word. Step 2: drop 'does' and change 'work' to 'works'.

questions.q: Rewrite as an indirect question beginning with 'Have you any idea ...': *When did the bus leave?*
options: Have you any idea when the bus left?
Have you any idea when did the bus leave?
Have you any idea when the bus leave?
Have you any idea when does the bus left?
questions.topic: Have you any idea ... + did → past simple
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: We start with the phrase 'Have you any idea', then drop 'did' and put the main verb in the past: 'left'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect question for: *When does the train leave?*
options: Could you tell me when the train leaves?
Could you tell me when does the train leave?
Could you tell me when leaves the train?
Could you tell me when the train leave?
questions.topic: Word order in indirect questions: subject before verb
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: The helping verb 'does' is dropped and the subject comes before the verb: 'the train leaves'.

questions.q: Change into an indirect question: *Does she speak French?*
options: I wonder if she speaks French.
I wonder if does she speak French.
I wonder that she speaks French.
I wonder if she speak French.
questions.topic: Using if for yes/no questions
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: A yes/no question becomes indirect with 'if' plus statement order: 'if she speaks French'.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: *Do you know what time the film ____?* (start)
options: starts
start
is start
starting
questions.topic: Third person -s after the subject in indirect questions
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: 'The film' is third person singular, so the verb takes -s: 'the film starts'.

questions.q: Only one of these sentences is written correctly. Which one?
options: I'd like to know where the ticket office is.
I'd like to know where the ticket office is?
I'd like to know where is the ticket office.
I'd like to know where the ticket office are.
questions.topic: Punctuation: an indirect question ends with a full stop
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: An indirect question is a statement, so it ends with a full stop and keeps subject-before-verb order.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *She asked me where is the nearest hospital.*
options: Because the subject comes before the verb: 'where the nearest hospital is'.
Because 'asked' should be followed by the word 'that'.
Because a question word cannot follow 'asked me'.
Because 'the nearest hospital' needs no article.
questions.topic: Explaining the word-order error after a reporting verb
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: After 'She asked me' the words follow statement order: 'where the nearest hospital is'.

questions.q: What is the difference between *When did they arrive?* and *I wonder when they arrived*?
options: The first is a direct question; the second is indirect with statement word order.
The first is indirect; the second is a direct question.
Both are direct questions, but the second is more polite.
Both are indirect questions, but the first ends with a question mark.
questions.topic: Difference between direct and indirect questions
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: The direct question puts 'did' before the subject; after 'I wonder' the order becomes a statement.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly reports this question? *Why did the team lose the match?*
options: She asked me why the team lost the match.
She asked me why did the team lose the match.
She asked me why the team did lost the match.
She asked me why lost the team the match.
questions.topic: Tense change after a past reporting verb (did → past simple)
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: 'Did' is dropped and the verb becomes past simple 'lost' after the past reporting verb 'asked'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect form of: *How many students are in the class?*
options: Could you tell me how many students are in the class?
Could you tell me how many students are the class in?
Could you tell me how many are students in the class?
Could you tell me how many students in the class are?
questions.topic: Indirect questions with 'how many'
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: After 'how many students' the sentence continues in statement order: 'are in the class'.

questions.q: Change into an indirect question: *Where can visitors park their cars?*
options: I'm not sure where visitors can park their cars.
I'm not sure where can visitors park their cars.
I'm not sure where visitors can to park their cars.
I'm not sure where do visitors can park their cars.
questions.topic: Keeping the modal 'can' in an indirect question
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: The modal 'can' stays, but the subject moves before it: 'where visitors can park their cars'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *Do you remember when does the museum open?*
options: Do you remember when the museum opens?
Do you remember when does the museum open?
Do you remember when the museum open?
Do you remember when does the museum opens?
questions.topic: Removing 'does' and adding -s in an indirect question
questions.lesson: Direct and indirect questions with question words | الأسئلة المباشرة وغير المباشرة بأدوات الاستفهام
questions.why: 'Does' is removed and the verb takes -s: 'when the museum opens'.

Language review 2 › Some tenses - التعبي.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)

questions.q: Which structure do we use to make the future of *can*?
options: will + be able to + infinitive
will + can + infinitive
will + have to + infinitive
will + must + infinitive
questions.topic: will + be able to (the future of can)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: can has no future form, so the future of ability is made with will + be able to + infinitive.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *I'm taking an exam at seven, so I ____ be able to answer the phone.*
options: won't
can't
don't
haven't
questions.topic: won't be able to (negative future ability)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: The negative future of can is won't be able to; can't be able to is not possible in English.

questions.q: Which structure do we use to make the future of *must*?
options: will + have to + infinitive
will + must + infinitive
will + be able to + infinitive
will + has to + infinitive
questions.topic: will + have to (the future of must)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: must has no future form, so the future of necessity is made with will + have to + infinitive.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The children ____ go to school on Friday because it is a holiday.*
options: won't have to
won't must
won't has to
not will have to
questions.topic: won't have to (no future necessity)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: The negative future of must is won't have to, meaning it will not be necessary.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *She will can drive a car next year.*
options: Because can has no future form, so we use will be able to
Because can is used only in negative sentences
Because will is used only with the third person
Because can must follow the infinitive in English
questions.topic: why 'will can' is not possible
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: We cannot put will before can; the future of can is will be able to + infinitive.

questions.q: Which sentence expresses future necessity, not future ability?
options: Visitors will have to leave their bags at the door.
Visitors will be able to leave their bags at the door.
Visitors will leave their bags at the door.
Visitors have left their bags at the door.
questions.topic: future necessity vs future ability
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: will have to shows that something will be necessary, while will be able to shows ability.

questions.q: What does this sentence mean? *Because of the storm, the plane won't be able to land in Aden tonight.*
options: The plane will not have the ability to land in Aden tonight.
It will not be necessary for the plane to land in Aden tonight.
The plane is not allowed to land in Aden tonight.
The plane must not land in Aden tonight.
questions.topic: meaning of 'won't be able to' in context
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: won't be able to is the negative future of can, so it means the plane will not have the ability to land.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *You will must show your passport at the airport.*
options: You will have to show your passport at the airport.
You will must to show your passport at the airport.
You must will show your passport at the airport.
You will have show your passport at the airport.
questions.topic: correcting 'will must' to 'will have to'
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: must has no future form, so will must is replaced by will have to + infinitive.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence in the future, keeping the same meaning: *He can't play in the match on Saturday.*
options: He won't be able to play in the match on Saturday.
He won't can play in the match on Saturday.
He won't have to play in the match on Saturday.
He doesn't be able to play in the match on Saturday.
questions.topic: turning 'can't' into the negative future
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: The future of can is will be able to, so can't becomes won't be able to.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence in the future, keeping the same meaning: *We must book the tickets before Friday.*
options: We will have to book the tickets before Friday.
We will must book the tickets before Friday.
We will have book the tickets before Friday.
We will be able to book the tickets before Friday.
questions.topic: turning 'must' into the future with will have to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: must has no future form, so must becomes will have to + infinitive.

questions.q: Which structure is used to talk about a certain future event in a formal way, especially in news and announcements?
options: be + to + infinitive
going to + infinitive
will be able to + infinitive
will have to + infinitive
questions.topic: be + to + infinitive for formal future events
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: be + to + infinitive expresses a certain future event in a formal way, as in news and announcements.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the form that shows a plan already decided: *A: Why did you buy all these medical books? B: I ____ study medicine at university.*
options: am going to
am to
will be able to
will have to
questions.topic: going to + infinitive for intentions
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: going to + infinitive is used for an intention or plan that was decided before speaking.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *After the six-month course, you ____ speak English fluently.*
options: will be able to
will can
will to can
are able to
questions.topic: will be able to as the future of can
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: can has no future form with will, so the future of can is will be able to.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *If you travel to Egypt next summer, you ____ get a visa first.*
options: will have to
will must
will can
will has to
questions.topic: will have to as the future of must
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: must has no future form with will, so the future of must is will have to.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *A: The phone is ringing! B: Don't worry, I ____ answer it.*
options: will
am going to
am to
will be able to
questions.topic: will for instant decisions
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: will is used for a decision made at the moment of speaking.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Ahmed looks very tired and keeps yawning. He ____ fall asleep in class.*
options: is going to
will
is to
will be able to
questions.topic: going to for predictions based on present evidence
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: going to is used for a prediction when we have evidence in front of us now.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The old market is to ____ next month to make room for a new hospital.*
options: close
closing
closed
closes
questions.topic: infinitive after be + to (not -ing or past form)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: After 'be to' we use the base form of the verb, so we say 'is to close', not 'is to closing'.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence in the future: *Sara can play the piano well, and she must practise every day.*
options: Sara will be able to play the piano well, and she will have to practise every day.
Sara will can play the piano well, and she will must practise every day.
Sara will be able to play the piano well, and she will must practise every day.
Sara will have to play the piano well, and she will be able to practise every day.
questions.topic: changing can and must into their future forms
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: The future of can is will be able to and the future of must is will have to.

questions.q: Combine the two sentences in one, using 'going to have to': *Our rent has gone up. We must move to a smaller flat.*
options: We're going to have to move to a smaller flat.
We're going to must move to a smaller flat.
We're going to have to moving to a smaller flat.
We're going to has to move to a smaller flat.
questions.topic: joining going to with have to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - التعبير عن المستقبل (will be able to / will have to / going to / be to)
questions.why: going to can be followed by have to to express a future obligation.

questions.q: What is a question tag?
options: A short question added to the end of a statement to make it a question
A short answer that comes after a question to confirm its meaning
A question word placed at the beginning of a statement
A short phrase added to the front of a sentence to attract attention
