questions.topic: Definition of a question tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: The lesson defines it as a short question we add at the end of a statement, turning that statement into a question.

questions.q: How is a question tag formed?
options: An auxiliary verb (be, do, have or a modal) followed by a pronoun
A main verb followed by the full subject of the statement
A question word followed by an auxiliary verb and a noun
An auxiliary verb followed by the object of the statement
questions.topic: Form of a question tag: auxiliary + pronoun
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: The book says we form a question tag using be, do, have or a modal followed by a pronoun.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *The film was very long, ____?*
options: wasn't it
was it
weren't they
didn't it
questions.topic: Using the verb be in the question tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: The statement has the verb 'was', so the tag uses the same verb in the negative with the pronoun 'it': wasn't it.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *This is your new bicycle, ____?*
options: isn't it
is not it
isn't he
doesn't it
questions.topic: Contracted form in a negative tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: A negative tag is always contracted (isn't), never 'is not', and the pronoun for 'this' is 'it'.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *Sami doesn't like fish, ____?*
options: does he
doesn't he
is he
did he
questions.topic: Negative statement takes a positive tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: When the verb in the statement is negative, the verb in the tag is positive, so 'doesn't' becomes 'does'.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *The man in the blue car is your uncle, ____?*
options: isn't he
isn't it
isn't the man
doesn't he
questions.topic: Pronoun that refers back to the subject
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: The tag uses a pronoun referring to the subject, so the long subject 'the man in the blue car' becomes 'he'.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *The bus had already left, ____?*
options: hadn't it
had it
didn't it
hasn't it
questions.topic: Using have / has / had as the auxiliary in the tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: When have/has/had is the auxiliary in the statement, the same auxiliary is used in the tag: hadn't it.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when are question tags used?
options: In spoken English or informal writing, when we want someone to agree with us
In formal reports and academic writing, when we introduce a new idea
In written English only, when we ask a stranger for information
In examination answers, when we want to make a statement stronger
questions.topic: When question tags are used: speech and informal writing
questions.lesson: Question tags - المعنى وطريقة التكوين
questions.why: The lesson says we use them only in spoken or informal written English, when we want someone to agree with what we are saying.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: *The students shouldn't be late for the exam, ____?*

doesn't it
has it

questions.q: What does 'mustn't' express in a sentence?
options: That an action is not allowed
That an action is not necessary
That a person is free to do or not to do it
That a person is unable to do it

questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: The lesson says mustn't means something is not allowed, so the action is forbidden.

questions.q: What does 'don't have to' express in a sentence?
options: That an action is not necessary and the person is free to choose
That an action is forbidden by a rule
That the person has no choice at all
That the person is not able to do the action
questions.topic: Meaning of don't have to (no necessity)
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: The lesson says don't have to means it is not necessary: you do it or you don't.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *Visitors ____ touch the paintings in the museum.*
options: mustn't
don't have to
doesn't have to
not have to
questions.topic: Using mustn't for rules that forbid
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: Touching the paintings is forbidden, so the rule needs mustn't, not don't have to.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My sister ____ have to cook tonight because we are eating in a restaurant.*
options: doesn't
don't
isn't
hasn't
questions.topic: Form: doesn't have to with he/she/it
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: With he, she and it the negative form is doesn't have to.

questions.q: Compare: *You mustn't bring food into the science lab.* / *You don't have to bring food into the science lab.* Which statement is correct?
options: The first forbids bringing food; the second says it is your choice
Both sentences forbid bringing food
Both sentences say bringing food is not necessary
The first gives a choice; the second forbids bringing food
questions.topic: Contrast: prohibition vs free choice
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: mustn't forbids the action, while don't have to means the action is simply not necessary.

questions.q: Read: *You don't have to wear a suit to the interview, but you mustn't wear jeans.* What does this tell the interviewee?
options: A suit is a free choice, but jeans are not allowed
A suit is not allowed, but jeans are a free choice
Both a suit and jeans are not allowed
Both a suit and jeans are free choices
questions.topic: Free choice and prohibition in one sentence
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: don't have to leaves the suit as a choice, and mustn't makes jeans forbidden.

questions.q: Read the sign on the train: *Passengers mustn't open the doors while the train is moving.* What does the sign mean?
options: Opening the doors is forbidden
Opening the doors is not necessary
Passengers are free to open the doors
Passengers are unable to open the doors
questions.topic: Reading rules and notices with mustn't
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: The sign forbids opening the doors, so mustn't is the right form for a rule.

questions.q: The lesson gives an easy way to remember the two forms. Complete it: *mustn't = no; don't have to = ____*

not allowed
not possible
not finished
questions.topic: Memory tip: mustn't = no, don't have to = not necessary
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: The lesson's tip is mustn't = 'no' and don't have to = 'not necessary'.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence with the same meaning, using 'mustn't' or 'don't have to': *It is not necessary for visitors to book a ticket in advance.*

Visitors doesn't have to book a ticket in advance.

Students must don't leave the classroom before the bell rings.
questions.topic: Rewriting a prohibition with mustn't
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Visitors ____ feed the animals in the zoo. It is not allowed.

don't have to
didn't have to
doesn't have to
questions.topic: using mustn't for a rule that forbids
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: Feeding the animals is forbidden, so the correct form is mustn't.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Our teacher ____ work on Saturday because the school is closed.
options: doesn't have to
don't have to
mustn't
didn't have to
questions.topic: the form doesn't have to with he/she/it

questions.why: With he/she/it we use doesn't have to, and the meaning here is no necessity.

questions.q: Complete both gaps: You ____ bring your own racket — the club gives you one. But you ____ throw rubbish on the court.

mustn't / mustn't
questions.topic: contrasting don't have to with mustn't
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to

mustn't
doesn't have to

questions.why: The no-necessity is in the past, so the correct form is didn't have to.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *Sara mustn't to go out alone at night.*
options: Sara mustn't go out alone at night.
Sara mustn't to going out alone at night.
Sara doesn't must go out alone at night.
Sara mustn't going out alone at night.
questions.topic: the error mustn't + to
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: After mustn't we use the bare infinitive: mustn't go, never mustn't to go.

questions.q: Which sentence is NOT correct?
options: My father don't have to work on Friday.
My sister doesn't have to cook tonight.
You mustn't smoke in the classroom.
They didn't have to pay for the bus.
questions.topic: the error He don't have to
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: With he/she/it we say doesn't have to, not don't have to.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: *It is not necessary for Ali to come early, but parking his car here is forbidden.*
options: Ali doesn't have to come early, but he mustn't park his car here.
Ali mustn't come early, but he doesn't have to park his car here.
Ali doesn't have to come early, but he doesn't have to park his car here.
Ali mustn't come early, but he mustn't park his car here.
questions.topic: rewriting two meanings with don't have to and mustn't
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: "not necessary" becomes doesn't have to, and "forbidden" becomes mustn't.

questions.q: Complete about last week: The museum was free for students, so we ____ pay, but the guard told us that we ____ touch the paintings.
options: didn't have to / mustn't

didn't have to / don't have to
questions.topic: past no necessity plus prohibition in one context
questions.lesson: Expressing obligation and necessity - الفرق بين mustn't و don't have to
questions.why: No necessity in the past is didn't have to, and a prohibition is mustn't.

questions.q: Choose the correct word order: *Salma / reads / the newspaper / every morning*

questions.topic: Word order in statements
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: In a statement the subject comes first, then the verb, then the object, then the rest of the sentence.

questions.q: In an English question, where does the subject come?
options: After the auxiliary verb
Before the auxiliary verb
After the main verb
At the end of the sentence
questions.topic: Position of the subject in a question
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.q: Complete the question: *____ your sister like reading stories?*

Do
Is
Has
questions.topic: Does in a Yes/No question
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: The subject 'your sister' is third person singular, so the question begins with Does and the verb stays in the base form.

questions.q: Complete the question: *Where ____ your parents yesterday?*
options: were
was
did
are
questions.topic: Wh- question with the verb be
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: After the question word, the verb be comes before the subject, and 'parents' is plural, so we use were.

questions.q: Compare: *The children were in the garden.* / *Were the children in the garden?* What changes when we make the question?
options: The verb were moves in front of the subject.
The subject moves to the end of the sentence.
We add did before the subject and use the base verb.
Nothing changes; the two sentences have the same order.
questions.topic: Statement and question with the verb be
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: With the verb be, a question is made by putting the verb before the subject, without adding do or did.

questions.q: Why is *Can you speak French?* correct while *Do you can speak French?* is wrong?
options: Can is an auxiliary verb, so it moves before the subject and needs no do.
Can is a main verb, so it needs the extra auxiliary do in questions.
A question in English must always begin with a question word.
Speak is a past tense verb, so it cannot come after the modal can.
questions.topic: Modal verb in a question
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.q: Complete the question: *____ invented the telephone?*

Who did
Whom did
Who does
questions.topic: Who asking about the subject
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: When Who asks about the subject itself, we do not add do/does/did; the word order stays subject + verb.

questions.topic: Order of two objects in a statement
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: After the verb, the indirect object (her friend) comes before the direct object (a letter).

questions.q: Change this statement into a question: *Nadia finished her homework before dinner.*

Did Nadia finished her homework before dinner?
Does Nadia finished her homework before dinner?
Nadia did finish her homework before dinner?
questions.topic: Forming a question from a statement
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: The past simple needs Did before the subject, and the main verb returns to the base form (finish).

questions.q: Change this statement into a question beginning with Where: *The students were sitting in the library.*

Where did the students sitting?

questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: The question word comes first, then the verb be, then the subject: Where + were + the students.

questions.q: In an indirect question, what is the correct order of words?
options: Introductory phrase + Wh-word + subject + verb
Introductory phrase + Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + verb
Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + verb
Auxiliary + subject + verb
questions.topic: Word order in indirect questions
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: An indirect question returns to the statement order: intro + Wh-word + subject + verb, and do/does/did are dropped.

questions.q: Make a yes/no question: *Layla can drive a car.*
options: Can Layla drive a car?
Does Layla can drive a car?
Layla can drive a car?
Can Layla drives a car?
questions.topic: Forming a yes/no question with the modal can
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined words: *They finished the project __last night__.*

When they finished the project?

When do they finish the project?
questions.topic: Forming Wh- questions with did

questions.why: The order is Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + base verb, so 'did' takes 'finish' and not 'finished'.

questions.q: Which sentence has the correct statement word order?

Does my father work in a hospital?
My father work in a hospital.
Works my father in a hospital.
questions.topic: Word order in statements
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال
questions.why: A statement follows subject + verb, so 'My father works in a hospital' is correct; the others are a question or have wrong order.

questions.q: What is the difference between the word order of a direct Wh- question and an indirect Wh- question?

The direct question puts the subject before the verb, but the indirect question puts the auxiliary before the subject.
Both the direct question and the indirect question put the auxiliary before the subject.
The indirect question uses do, does or did, but the direct question does not.

questions.q: Why is this sentence incorrect? *Do you know where is the station?*

Because the sentence needs 'did' instead of 'is'.

questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.q: Choose the correct yes/no question: *The children play football after school.*
options: Do the children play football after school?

Do the children plays football after school?
The children play football after school?
questions.topic: Choosing do or does in yes/no questions
questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

Do you know where the team practise?

questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

questions.q: Change into an indirect question beginning with 'Could you tell me': *Where can I find a bank?*

questions.lesson: Word order in statements and questions | ترتيب الكلمات في الجملة الخبرية والسؤال

You don't eat too much sugar.
Doesn't eat too much sugar.
questions.topic: Turning a negative suggestion into a negative imperative
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: First drop the subject and the modal, then make it negative with Don't + the infinitive.

questions.q: Turn the suggestion *You could try our fresh juice.* into a direct imperative for an advertisement.
options: Try our fresh juice!
You try our fresh juice!
Trying our fresh juice!
Could try our fresh juice!
questions.topic: Turning a 'could' suggestion into an advertisement imperative
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: Remove the subject and the modal “could” and keep the bare infinitive, as advertisements do.

questions.q: Which of these sentences is the strongest way to tell someone to do something?
options: Finish your homework now!
You should finish your homework now.
Why not finish your homework now?
You could finish your homework now.
questions.topic: The imperative as the strongest form
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: The imperative (the verb with no subject) is the strongest form; 'should', 'Why not ...?' and 'could' are all gentler than it.

questions.q: Which sentence makes the gentlest, least forceful suggestion?
options: Take a short break!
You should take a short break.
You could take a short break.
Why not take a short break?
questions.topic: You could: the gentlest suggestion
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'You could' is the lightest of the four patterns, so it suggests without pressing the listener.

questions.q: Complete the suggestion with the correct form: *Why not ____ your umbrella? It's raining.*
options: to take
take
taking
takes
questions.topic: Why not + bare infinitive
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'Why not' is always followed by the bare infinitive, so we say 'Why not take ...?' not 'Why not to take'.

questions.q: Complete the advice with the correct form: *You should ____ a warm jacket; it is cold outside.*
options: wear
to wear
wearing
wears
questions.topic: You should + bare infinitive
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'Should' is a modal verb, so the verb that follows it is the bare infinitive: 'You should wear ...'.

questions.q: Which of these is a suggestion, NOT an order?
options: Join the science club!
Bring your notebook tomorrow.
Don't be late again!
You could join the science club.
questions.topic: Suggestions vs orders
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'You could ...' only suggests, while the other three are imperatives, which give a direct order.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *Why not to take a taxi to the airport?*
options: Why not taking a taxi to the airport?
Why not take a taxi to the airport?
Why not to take a taxi to the airport?
Why not you take a taxi to the airport?
questions.topic: Common error: Why not to + verb
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: After 'Why not' we use the bare infinitive, so the 'to' must be deleted: 'Why not take ...?'

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *You visit our new shop in Sana'a!*
options: You visiting our new shop in Sana'a!
To visit our new shop in Sana'a!
Visit our new shop in Sana'a!
You should visiting our new shop in Sana'a!
questions.topic: The imperative takes no subject
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: An imperative has no subject, so the pronoun must be dropped: 'Visit our new shop in Sana'a!'

questions.q: Which sentence means the same as *Why not revise for the exam with a friend?*
options: Why you don't revise for the exam with a friend?
Why not to revise for the exam with a friend?
Why don't you revise for the exam with a friend?
You should to revise for the exam with a friend?
questions.topic: Why don't you = Why not
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'Why don't you + verb' is another form with the same meaning as 'Why not + verb'.

questions.q: Change this order into a gentle suggestion with 'You could': *See a dentist this week.*
options: You could to see a dentist this week.
You could see a dentist this week.
You could seeing a dentist this week.
You could saw a dentist this week.
questions.topic: Changing an order into a polite suggestion
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'Could' takes the bare infinitive, so the imperative 'See a dentist this week' becomes 'You could see a dentist this week'.

questions.q: Change the advice into a question-suggestion, keeping the same verb form: *You should save some money every month.*
options: Why not to save some money every month?
Why don't save some money every month?
Why not saving some money every month?
Why not save some money every month?
questions.topic: Changing 'You should' into 'Why not ...?'
questions.lesson: Giving advice and making suggestions | تقديم النصيحة والاقتراح (الأمر / Why not / should / could)
questions.why: 'You should + verb' becomes the gentler 'Why not + the same bare verb', so the verb 'save' does not change.

Language review 3 › Question tags - حالا.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *I am the first person to arrive, ____?*
options: aren't I
amn't I
am I
don't I
questions.topic: Question tag after 'I am' (aren't I)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson states 'I am ← aren't I', as in 'I'm late, aren't I?' — 'amn't I' is never used.

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *Let's visit the museum on Friday, ____?*
options: shall we
will we
don't we
aren't we
questions.topic: Question tag after 'Let's' (shall we)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson gives 'Let's ← shall we': Let's go, shall we?

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *There are two hospitals in our town, ____?*
options: aren't there
aren't they
isn't there
don't they
questions.topic: Question tag with 'There is / There are'
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson says 'There is / There are ← we use there', so the tag repeats there and agrees: aren't there?

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *Khalid never eats breakfast before nine, ____?*
options: does he
doesn't he
did he
is he
questions.topic: Negative words (never, hardly, nobody) take a positive tag
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson says never / hardly / nobody make the sentence negative, so the tag must be positive: does he?

questions.q: Read the sentence *So you have finished your project, have you?* Why does the speaker use a positive tag after a positive statement?
options: To show interest or surprise, not to ask for agreement
To ask the listener to agree with the statement
To show that the speaker thinks the statement is untrue
To turn the statement into a polite order
questions.topic: Positive statement + positive tag to show interest
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson explains that a positive tag after a positive statement shows interest or is just polite — no agreement is being asked for.

questions.q: Which sentence has the correct question tag?
options: Nobody in the village knew the news, did they?
Nobody in the village knew the news, did it?
Nothing in the village was open, were they?
Everybody in the village was asleep, wasn't it?
questions.topic: Pronoun in the tag after nobody / everybody (they)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson: nobody / everybody / somebody take they, while nothing / everything take it, so 'did they?' is the correct tag.

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *Please pass me the salt, ____?*
options: will you
shall we
do you
aren't you
questions.topic: Question tag after imperatives (will you / won't you)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: An imperative takes will you? or won't you? as in the lesson's 'Close the door, will you?'

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the tag: *These pictures on the wall are yours, ____?*
options: aren't they
isn't it
aren't these
don't they
questions.topic: Pronoun in the tag after these / those (they)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson gives this / that → it and these / those → they, so 'These ...' takes aren't they?

questions.q: Add the correct question tag to *Nobody has finished the homework.* Which full sentence is correct?
options: Nobody has finished the homework, have they?
Nobody has finished the homework, hasn't they?
Nobody has finished the homework, has it?
Nobody has finished the homework, haven't they?
questions.topic: Two-step tag: negative word nobody + present perfect
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: Two steps: nobody is a negative word so the tag is positive, and nobody takes they — giving 'have they?'

questions.q: Add the correct question tag to *There is nothing to worry about.* Which full sentence is correct?
options: There is nothing to worry about, is there?
There is nothing to worry about, isn't there?
There is nothing to worry about, is it?
There is nothing to worry about, isn't it?
questions.topic: Two-step tag: negative word 'nothing' + 'there'
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: Two steps: nothing makes the sentence negative (so a positive tag), and 'There is' repeats there — giving 'is there?'

questions.q: In a tag question, what does a falling voice (↘) at the end tell us about the speaker?
options: The speaker is sure of the facts and only wants agreement
The speaker is not sure and is really asking a question
The speaker wants the listener to repeat the whole statement
The speaker is asking for a long answer, not a short one
questions.topic: falling intonation ↘ (certainty)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: A falling voice (↘) means the speaker is certain and only wants agreement, as in “It’s hot today, isn’t it? ↘”.

questions.q: Your friend says: *“You've finished your homework, haven't you? ↗”* What does the rising voice tell you?
options: She is not sure about it and really wants to know
She is sure about it and only wants you to agree
She is ordering you to finish your homework quickly
She has already checked your homework and is pleased
questions.topic: rising intonation ↗ (uncertainty)
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: A rising voice (↗) means the speaker is not sure and is asking a real question, as the lesson explains.

questions.q: Your sister says: *“Maha won't come to the party, will she?”* In fact, Maha is coming. What is the correct answer?
options: Yes, she will.
No, she won't.
Yes, she won't.
No, she will.
questions.topic: answering a tag question by the fact
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The lesson says we answer according to the fact, not the shape of the question: she is coming, so “Yes, she will.”

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *There is a bank near our school, isn't it?*
options: There is a bank near our school, isn't there?
There is a bank near our school, is it?
There is a bank near our school, aren't there?
There is a bank near our school, doesn't it?
questions.topic: tag after There is / There are
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The tag of “There is …” is “isn’t there?”, and “isn’t it?” is listed among the lesson’s common errors.

questions.q: Complete the dialogue: *A: Your father hasn't come home yet, ____? B: No, he ____.*
options: has he — hasn't
hasn't he — has
does he — doesn't
has he — has
questions.topic: question tag + short answer in a dialogue
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The statement is negative (“hasn’t”), so the tag is positive “has he?”, and the true short answer is “No, he hasn’t.”

questions.q: Your teacher says: *“You have brought your books, haven't you? ↗”* You have brought them. What does her voice show, and what do you answer?
options: She is not sure, so I answer: “Yes, I have.”
She is sure, so I answer: “Yes, I have.”
She is not sure, so I answer: “No, I haven't.”
She is sure, so I answer: “No, I haven't.”
questions.topic: combining ↗ intonation with the short answer
questions.lesson: Question tags - حالات خاصة وطريقة النطق
questions.why: The rising voice (↗) shows she is not sure, and since the fact is true the answer is “Yes, I have.”

Language review 4 › Sequence words | كلم.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)

questions.q: Complete the sequence with the correct word: *____, wash the car with water. Next, clean the windows. Then dry it with a clean cloth.*
options: First
Finally
After that
Then
questions.topic: First introduces the first event
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says a sequence must begin with First, and the other words come after it.

questions.q: According to the lesson, which word must end a sequence of events?
options: Finally
After that
Next
Then
questions.topic: Finally ends a sequence
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says we must begin with First and end with Finally.

questions.q: When do we use words like First, Next, Then, After that and Finally?
options: When we describe events in the order they happen
When we compare two people or things
When we ask a question about the past
When we give a reason for an action
questions.topic: the use of sequence words
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says we use these words to introduce the events when we describe a sequence of events.

questions.q: What does 'After that' mean in a sequence?
options: The event comes after the one before it
The event comes before all the others
The event is the last one in the sequence
The event happens at the same time as another
questions.topic: the meaning of After that
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: In the lesson 'After that' means the next event, after the one just mentioned.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'After that' and 'Finally'?
options: 'After that' adds another event; 'Finally' introduces the last one
'After that' introduces the last event; 'Finally' adds another one
'After that' begins the sequence; 'Finally' is used in the middle
'After that' is used in questions; 'Finally' is used in answers
questions.topic: the difference between After that and Finally
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: After that may come in any order in the middle, but the sequence must end with Finally.

questions.q: Which of these words cannot change its place in a sequence? *Next / Then / After that / Finally*
options: Finally
Next
Then
After that
questions.topic: the fixed place of Finally
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says Next, Then and After that can come in any order, but the sequence ends with Finally.

questions.q: Why is a comma used in this sentence? *First, the students read the text carefully.*
options: Because a comma usually comes after First, Next, After that and Finally
Because the sentence is a question about the past
Because First is the last word of the sequence
Because a comma always comes after Then
questions.topic: the comma after First
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says we usually put a comma after First, Next, After that and Finally.

questions.q: Which word is usually written without a comma after it? *First, ... / Then ... / After that, ... / Finally, ...*
options: Then
First
After that
Finally
questions.topic: Then is usually written without a comma
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson notes that Then is usually written without a comma, unlike the other sequence words.

questions.q: Which change makes this sequence correct? *Then we reached the airport. First, we checked in our bags. After that, we waited at the gate. Finally, we got on the plane.*
options: Move 'First' to the beginning, before 'Then'
Move 'Finally' to the beginning of the sequence
Change 'After that' to 'First' and keep the other words in their places
Change 'Then' to 'Finally' and keep the other words in their places
questions.topic: First must open the sequence
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: A sequence must begin with First, so First has to come before Then.

questions.q: Re-order these sentences to make a good sequence: *(A) Finally, they thanked the doctor.* *(B) First, Ali fell off his bike and hurt his leg.* *(C) After that, the doctor gave him some medicine.* *(D) Then his father took him to the hospital.*
options: B, D, C, A
B, C, D, A
D, B, C, A
B, D, A, C
questions.topic: ordering a story with First, Then, After that, Finally
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: First (B) opens the sequence, the hospital (D) comes before the medicine (C), and Finally (A) ends it.

questions.q: Choose the sequence word that begins this set of steps: *____ , I filled the kettle and made tea. Next, I washed the cups.*
options: First
Later
Afterwards
Lastly
questions.topic: The opening word of a sequence
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: Only 'First' opens a sequence; the other three words can only come after the first step.

questions.q: What does the word 'Finally' tell us about a step?
options: It is the last step of the sequence
It is the first step of the sequence
It happens at the same time as another step
It shows the reason for the step before it
questions.topic: Meaning of Finally
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: 'Finally' always marks the last step, so no step can come after it.

questions.q: Complete with the correct sequence word: *Next, we cleaned the classroom. ____ , we watered the flowers in the yard.*
options: Then
At first
To begin with
At the end of
questions.topic: Then after Next
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: 'Then' joins a step that follows another step; the other three words cannot follow 'Next'.

questions.q: Where do 'Afterwards' and 'Later' come in a sequence?
options: In the middle, after the first step
Only at the very beginning of the sequence
Only at the very end of the sequence
Before the word 'First'
questions.topic: Position of Afterwards and Later
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson lists 'Afterwards' and 'Later' as middle words, like 'Secondly'.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'In the end' and 'At the end of'?
options: 'In the end' means finally after a long time, but 'At the end of' shows the last part of something
'In the end' is used for the first step, but 'At the end of' is used for the middle step
'In the end' is used only in speech, but 'At the end of' is used only in writing
'In the end' is followed by a verb, but 'At the end of' is followed by a person
questions.topic: In the end vs At the end of
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: 'In the end' means after waiting or trying, while 'At the end of' refers to the last part of something, as in 'at the end of the lesson'.

questions.q: Why is this opening wrong? *Finally, I opened the shop and turned on the lights.*
options: Because 'Finally' marks the last step, so it cannot open a sequence
Because 'Finally' is used only with the past simple
Because 'Finally' must be followed by a comma and a noun
Because 'Finally' means the same as 'Next'
questions.topic: Finally cannot open a sequence
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The lesson says 'Finally' is always the last step, so placing it at the beginning is a mistake.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: After that, I packed my bag and went to bed.
After that I afterwards, packed my bag and went to bed.
After that, then I packed my bag and went to bed.
After that, next I packed my bag and went to bed.
questions.topic: One sequence word per step
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: Each step takes only one order word; the other sentences repeat two order words in the same step.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *At first, I washed the car, then I cleaned the windows, and then I painted the door.*
options: Change 'At first' to 'First'
Change 'At first' to 'Lastly'
Change 'then' to 'firstly'
Change 'At first' to 'At the end of'
questions.topic: At first vs First
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: 'At first' describes a situation that changed later, but this sentence lists steps, so 'First' is the correct word.

questions.q: Re-order these steps into a correct paragraph: *the guests arrived / we cooked the food / everyone went home / we served dinner*
options: Firstly, we cooked the food. Secondly, the guests arrived. Afterwards, we served dinner. In the end, everyone went home.
Secondly, we cooked the food. Firstly, the guests arrived. Afterwards, everyone went home. In the end, we served dinner.
Firstly, everyone went home. Secondly, we served dinner. Afterwards, the guests arrived. In the end, we cooked the food.
In the end, we cooked the food. Firstly, we served dinner. Secondly, everyone went home. Afterwards, the guests arrived.
questions.topic: Ordering steps in a paragraph
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: The food must be cooked before the guests arrive, and they go home only after dinner, so the order is cook, arrive, serve, leave.

questions.q: Choose the best sentence to complete this paragraph: *Firstly, we chose the theme of our project. Secondly, we collected the information from the internet. ____*
options: Lastly, we wrote the report and handed it to our teacher.
Firstly, we wrote the report and handed it to our teacher.
To begin with, we wrote the report and handed it to our teacher.
Secondly, we wrote the report and handed it to our teacher.
questions.topic: Closing sentence with Lastly
questions.lesson: Sequence words | كلمات الترتيب (First / Next / Then / After that / Finally)
questions.why: 'Lastly' closes the list of steps, while the other three words belong to the beginning of a sequence.

Language review 4 › Word signposts | الك.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is a word signpost?
options: A word that tells the reader what kind of idea comes next
A word that tells the reader how a word is pronounced
A word that tells the reader where a story takes place
A word that tells the reader who is speaking in the text
questions.topic: the meaning of the term word signpost
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The lesson says these words act like signposts: they tell you what is coming next in the text.

questions.q: What do 'However' and 'On the other hand' have in common in this lesson?
options: They both introduce an idea that is different from the one before
They both introduce the result of the idea that came before
They both join two adjectives inside the same sentence
They both come at the end of a sentence after a comma
questions.topic: the shared function of contrast signposts
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Both of them introduce a contrast, so what follows is likely to differ from what came before.

questions.q: Which of these word signposts is used to show a result?
options: Therefore
However
On the other hand
But
questions.topic: words that introduce a result
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Therefore introduces a result, while However and On the other hand introduce a contrast.

questions.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The bag was expensive. However, she bought it.
The bag was expensive, however she bought it.
The bag was expensive however. She bought it.
The bag was expensive. However she, bought it.
questions.topic: punctuation of However
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: However usually starts a new sentence and a comma comes after it, so 'However, she bought it.' is right.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *Omar is a good student ____ he is sometimes careless.*
options: but
however
on the other hand
therefore
questions.topic: but joining two ideas inside one sentence
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: But joins two ideas inside the same sentence, while However and On the other hand start a new sentence.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word signpost: *The museum was closed. ____, we took photos of the old city from outside.*
options: However
Therefore
As a result
Because of this
questions.topic: choosing a contrast signpost in context
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The second idea is different from the first, so the sentence needs the contrast signpost However.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the word signpost that shows a result: *The team trained hard every day. ____, they won the final match.*
options: However
On the other hand
As a result
But
questions.topic: choosing a result signpost in context
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Winning the match is the result of training hard, so 'As a result' is the correct signpost.

questions.q: Read the sentences: *The road was very narrow and dark. Therefore, the driver went slowly.* What does the signpost 'Therefore' tell you?
options: The second idea is a result of the first
The second idea is different from the first
The second idea happened before the first
The second idea has no connection with the first
questions.topic: predicting the next idea from the signpost Therefore
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Therefore tells the reader that what comes next is the result of what came before.

questions.q: Rewrite the two sentences as one text with 'However' at the start of a new sentence, keeping the past tense: *The weather was very cold. The children played outside.*
options: The weather was very cold. However, the children played outside.
The weather was very cold. However, the children play outside.
The weather was very cold, however the children played outside.
The weather was very cold. However the children, played outside.
questions.topic: joining two sentences with However
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: However begins a new sentence, is followed by a comma, and the past tense 'played' stays the same.

questions.q: Read the text: *Hana wanted to buy the new phone. However, it was very expensive. As a result, she waited until the price went down.* What happened to Hana?
options: She waited and bought it later at a lower price
She bought it at once although it cost a lot
She never bought it because the price went up
She bought another phone that cost even more
questions.topic: following contrast and result signposts in a short text
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: 'However' shows the price was a problem, and 'As a result' shows she waited for a lower price.

questions.q: Complete the rule: The words 'Therefore', 'Because of this' and 'As a result' introduce ____ .
options: a result
a contrast
a reason
an example
questions.topic: The function of result signposts (Therefore / Because of this / As a result)
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The lesson states: 'Therefore, Because of this and As a result introduce a result.'

questions.q: Where does 'Therefore' come when it introduces a result?
options: At the beginning of a new sentence, followed by a comma
In the middle of a sentence, between two commas
At the end of a sentence, after the result
At the beginning of the second clause, joined to the first by a comma
questions.topic: Position and comma after 'Therefore'
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: It comes at the start of a new sentence and is followed by a comma, as in the book's own example.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: *The flight was delayed by fog. ____ , I missed my sister's wedding.*
options: As a result
However
On the other hand
Because

questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The fog is the cause and missing the wedding is the result, so a result signpost is needed.

questions.q: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: *The new laptop is quite heavy. ____ , it works very fast.*
options: On the other hand
On other hand
On the others hand
On an other hand
questions.topic: The correct written form of 'On the other hand'
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The error list gives 'On other hand' as wrong and 'On the other hand' as the correct form.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'therefore' and 'so'?
options: 'Therefore' begins a new sentence, but 'so' joins two clauses in the same sentence.
'So' begins a new sentence, but 'therefore' joins two clauses in the same sentence.
'Therefore' shows a contrast, but 'so' shows a result.
'So' is used in writing only, but 'therefore' is used in speech only.
questions.topic: The difference between 'therefore' and 'so'
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: 'So' joins its two clauses inside one sentence, while 'Therefore' starts a new sentence.

questions.q: In three of these sentences the signpost is used correctly. Which sentence uses the signpost wrongly?
options: Yousef practised every day. Therefore, he won the race.
The shop was closed. As a result, we could not buy any bread.
Hana was tired. However, she went to bed early.

questions.topic: Recognising a signpost that does not match the relation
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Being tired is the reason for going to bed early, so a result signpost is needed, not 'However'.

questions.q: Choose the signpost that keeps the same meaning: *The library was closed, so we studied at home.*
options: As a result
However
On the other hand
For example
questions.topic: Replacing 'so' with a result signpost
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: 'So' and 'As a result' both introduce a result; only the position in the sentence changes.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Solar panels are clean and save money. ____ , they do not work well on cloudy days.*
options: On the other hand
As a result
Therefore
Because of this
questions.topic: Using 'On the other hand' for the other side of an argument
questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: Cloudy days are the other side of the argument, so a contrast signpost is needed.

questions.q: Choose the best way to join the two sentences: *The bridge was damaged by the flood.* *The village was cut off for three days.*
options: The bridge was damaged by the flood. As a result, the village was cut off for three days.

The bridge was damaged by the flood. On the other hand, the village was cut off for three days.
The bridge was damaged by the flood. As a result the village was cut off for three days.

questions.lesson: Word signposts | الكلمات الإرشادية للتضاد والنتيجة (However / On the other hand / Therefore / As a result)
questions.why: The cutting off is the result of the flood, and the signpost must take a comma after it.

questions.q: Choose the signpost that shows the correct relation between the two sentences: *Our team lost its best player before the final.* *We still won the match by two goals.*
options: However
Therefore
As a result
Because of this

Language review 1 › Talking about the pa.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)

questions.q: When do we use the past perfect?
options: For an action that happened before another action in the past
For an action that has continued up to the present moment
For an action that will happen before another action in the future
For an action that was repeated regularly in the past
questions.topic: Use of the past perfect for an earlier past action
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The lesson says the past perfect is used for something that happened earlier than something else in the past.

questions.q: Which sentence is a correct past perfect question?
options: Did the students had finished the test?
Had the students finish the test?
Had the students finished the test?
Were the students had finished the test?
questions.topic: Question form of the past perfect (Had + subject + past participle)
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The past perfect question is Had + subject + past participle: Had the students finished?

questions.q: Write the negative form of this past perfect sentence: *She had seen the message before she left the office.*
options: She hadn't seen the message before she left the office.
She didn't see the message before she left the office.
She hasn't seen the message before she left the office.
She didn't had seen the message before she left the office.
questions.topic: Negative form of the past perfect (hadn't + past participle)
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The negative of the past perfect is hadn't + past participle, with the same form for all subjects.

questions.q: Which sentence tells us that the film started before we reached the cinema?
options: When we reached the cinema, the film had begun.
When we reached the cinema, the film began.
When we had reached the cinema, the film began.
When we reach the cinema, the film had begun.
questions.topic: Meaning difference: past simple vs past perfect with 'when'
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: 'Had begun' is the earlier action, so the film started first and we arrived after it.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *They had sold all the tickets before the concert ____ .* (begin)
options: had begun
began
has begun
begins
questions.topic: The verb after 'before' is in the past simple
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The verb after 'before' is in the past simple, while the earlier action carries the past perfect.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The team lost the game because they ____ enough.* (not practise)
options: haven't practised
didn't practised
hadn't practise
hadn't practised
questions.topic: 'because' introduces the earlier action in the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The reason happened first, so after 'because' we use the past perfect negative: hadn't practised.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *By the time the guests arrived, we ____ everything for the party.* (prepare)
options: have prepared
had prepare
had prepared
has prepared
questions.topic: 'by the time' with the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: With 'by the time' the earlier action takes the past perfect: we had prepared everything before they arrived.

questions.q: Join these two sentences with *After*: *The rain stopped. Then the children went out to play.*
options: After the rain had stopped, the children went out to play.
After the rain stopped, the children had gone out to play.
After the rain had stopped, the children had gone out to play.
After the rain has stopped, the children went out to play.
questions.topic: Joining two past sentences with 'after'
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The stopping of the rain is the earlier action, so it becomes the past perfect after 'after', and the later action stays past simple.

questions.q: Combine the two sentences with *because*: *It rained heavily during the night. The road was wet in the morning.*
options: The road was wet in the morning because it has rained heavily during the night.
The road had been wet in the morning because it rained heavily during the night.
The road was wet in the morning because it rains heavily during the night.
The road was wet in the morning because it had rained heavily during the night.
questions.topic: Joining two past sentences with 'because'
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The rain came first, so it takes the past perfect after 'because', and the result stays in the past simple.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *By the time we arrived at the hall, the guests ____ (leave).*
options: left
had left
have left
had leave
questions.topic: Form of the past perfect: had + past participle
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The guests left before we arrived, so the earlier action takes had + past participle: had left.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Sami was late for school because he ____ (not / wake) up on time.*
options: didn't woke
hadn't wake
hadn't woken
hasn't woken
questions.topic: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The negative past perfect is had not (hadn't) + the past participle: hadn't woken.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *After the rain had stopped, the children ____ out to play.*
options: went
had went
go
going
questions.topic: Tense of the second clause after 'after + past perfect'
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: After 'after + past perfect', the later action is in the past simple: had stopped ... went.

questions.q: Read the sentence and answer: *The road was closed because the storm __had damaged__ the bridge.* Why is the past perfect __had damaged__ used?
options: It shows that the storm damaged the bridge after the road was closed.
It shows that the two actions happened at the same time.
It shows that the action continued for a long time in the past.
It shows that the storm damaged the bridge before the road was closed.
questions.topic: Why the earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The storm damaged the bridge first, so that earlier action takes the past perfect had damaged.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *She had wrote the letter before the meeting began.*
options: She has written the letter before the meeting began.
She had written the letter before the meeting began.
She wrote the letter before the meeting had began.
She had write the letter before the meeting began.
questions.topic: Past participle of irregular verbs after had (write → written)
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: After had we use the past participle written, not the past simple wrote.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *When we reached the cinema, the film had ____ started.*
options: yet
ever
already
still
questions.topic: Using 'already' with the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: Already goes between had and the past participle to show the action happened sooner than expected.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: The plane had taken off before we reached the airport.
The plane had take off before we reached the airport.
The plane has taken off before we reached the airport.
The plane had taken off before we reach the airport.
questions.topic: Recognising correct and incorrect past perfect sentences
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The plane took off before we reached the airport, so had taken off (had + past participle) is correct.

questions.q: Rewrite as one sentence using 'after': *The team practised for months. Then they won the final.*
options: After the team had practised for months, they had won the final.
After the team practised for months, they had won the final.
After the team had practise for months, they won the final.
After the team had practised for months, they won the final.
questions.topic: Joining two past actions with 'after' and the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: The earlier action (practising) takes had + past participle; the later action (winning) takes the past simple.

questions.q: Rewrite the two sentences as one sentence beginning with 'Because': *Hana missed the bus. She was late for the exam.*
options: Because Hana had missed the bus, she had been late for the exam.
Because Hana had missed the bus, she was late for the exam.
Because Hana has missed the bus, she was late for the exam.
Because Hana had miss the bus, she was late for the exam.
questions.topic: Using the past perfect for the earlier event only when joining with 'because'
questions.lesson: Talking about the past - الماضي التام (حدث وقع قبل حدث آخر)
questions.why: Only the earlier action takes the past perfect: had missed ... she was late.

Language review 2 › Some tenses - used t.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)

questions.q: What does *used to + infinitive* show?
options: Something happened in the past but does not happen now
Something is happening at the moment of speaking
Something will certainly happen in the future
Something has happened many times up to now
questions.topic: Meaning of used to + infinitive
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The lesson says it shows that something happened in the past, but doesn't now.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My cousins ____ play volleyball on the beach every summer when they were children.*
options: use to
used to
used
using to
questions.topic: Affirmative form: used to + infinitive
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The form is 'used to + infinitive', and it stays the same with all pronouns.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My brother ____ use to get up early, but now he gets up at five.*
options: doesn't
don't
didn't
hasn't
questions.topic: Negative form: didn't use to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The negative is 'didn't use to', and 'use' is written without -d after 'didn't'.

questions.q: Complete the question: *____ your sister use to wear a uniform at primary school?*
options: Did
Does
Was
Has
questions.topic: Question form: Did + subject + use to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: Questions are made with 'Did + subject + use to + infinitive', so we begin with 'Did'.

questions.q: Read the sentence: *My father used to work in a hospital in Aden.* What does this tell us about him?
options: He worked in a hospital in the past, but he does not work there now
He works in a hospital in Aden now
He has never worked in a hospital
He will work in a hospital in Aden in the future
questions.topic: Meaning of used to in context (a situation that has ended)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: 'Used to' shows a past situation that is no longer true, so the work there has stopped.

questions.q: What is the difference between *She used to live in Ibb* and *She lives in Ibb*?
options: Both sentences are about the present
The first sentence is about the future, the second is about the past
The first sentence is about now, the second is about the past
The first sentence is about the past, the second is about now
questions.topic: Difference between used to and the present simple
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: 'Used to' describes a past situation that has ended, while the present simple describes what is true now.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My uncle never ____ to drink tea in the evening when he was young.*
options: use
used
uses
using
questions.topic: never used to + infinitive
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: With 'never' we keep the full form: 'He never used to drink tea.'

questions.q: What does the underlined word mean? *That shop used to be a __baker's__.*
options: a person whose job is making bread
a shop where people buy meat
a shop where bread is made and sold
a shop where people buy medicine
questions.topic: Meaning of a baker's (a baker's shop)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The lesson explains that 'a baker's' means 'a baker's shop', the shop of the baker.

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined words: *They used to play __football__ in the street every Friday.*
options: What did they use to play in the street every Friday?
What did they used to play in the street every Friday?
What do they use to play in the street every Friday?
What they used to play in the street every Friday?
questions.topic: Making a question with used to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The question needs 'did + subject + use to + infinitive', so we say 'did they use to play'.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence with 'never' and keep the same meaning: *My grandfather did not use to drink coffee.*
options: My grandfather never use to drink coffee.
My grandfather never used to drinking coffee.
My grandfather did never use to drank coffee.
My grandfather never used to drink coffee.
questions.topic: Rewriting didn't use to with never used to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: 'Never used to + infinitive' has the same meaning as 'did not use to', and 'used' keeps its -d.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My father used to ____ to work by bus before he bought a car.*
options: go
going
went
to go
questions.topic: used to + infinitive (form)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: After 'used to' we always use the base form of the verb: used to + go.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Sara is used to ____ with her left hand.*
options: writing
write
wrote
to write
questions.topic: be used to + -ing (form)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: After 'be used to' we use the -ing form: be used to + writing.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *He didn't ____ to enjoy reading, but now he loves it.*
options: use
used
using
uses
questions.topic: Negative form: didn't use to
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: In the negative we write 'didn't use to' + base form, not 'didn't used to'.

questions.q: What is the difference between these two sentences? *Salem worked in a bank.* / *Salem used to work in a bank.*
options: The second shows a habit that has now ended; the first only states a past fact
The first shows a habit that has now ended; the second states a present habit
The second shows that he still works in the bank now
Both sentences mean that he works in the bank now
questions.topic: Past simple vs 'used to'
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The past simple states a fact, while 'used to' adds the idea of a finished past habit.

questions.q: What does this sentence mean? *After a year in Cairo, Omar is used to driving in heavy traffic.*
options: Driving in heavy traffic is now normal for him
He drove in heavy traffic in the past but has stopped
He is learning to drive in heavy traffic now
He will drive in heavy traffic in the future
questions.topic: Meaning of 'be used to' (present)
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' means the action has become normal and easy for you now.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *My mother use to cook on a wood fire.*
options: 'Use to' is wrong; a finished past habit needs 'used to'
'Cook' must change to 'cooking' after 'used to'
The sentence needs 'is' before 'use to'
'My mother' is singular, so the verb must be 'uses to'
questions.topic: Common error: 'use to' instead of 'used to'
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The form for a finished past habit is always 'used to', never 'use to'.

questions.q: Make a question from this sentence: *They used to play football in the old stadium.*
options: Did they use to play football in the old stadium?
Did they used to play football in the old stadium?
Do they use to play football in the old stadium?
Were they used to play football in the old stadium?
questions.topic: Question form with 'used to'
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The question is: Did + subject + use to + base form.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence using 'used to' so that the meaning stays the same: *Salwa works in a bank now, but from 2015 to 2019 she worked in a school.*
options: Salwa used to work in a school.
Salwa is used to working in a school.
Salwa used to working in a school.
Salwa use to work in a school.
questions.topic: Rewriting a finished past job with 'used to'
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: The 2015-2019 job is a finished past habit, so 'used to work' is the correct form.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *We are used to walk to school every day now.*
options: We are used to walking to school every day now.
We used to walk to school every day now.
We are used to walked to school every day now.
We are use to walking to school every day now.
questions.topic: Common error: 'be used to' + base form
questions.lesson: Some tenses - used to (شيء كان يحدث في الماضي ولم يعد)
questions.why: 'Be used to' takes the -ing form, so 'walk' must become 'walking'.

he
it

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word: *The horse, ____ won the race, belongs to my cousin.*

it
he

questions.q: According to the lesson, what do we use a relative clause for?
options: To give extra information about someone or something
To ask a question about someone or something
To give an order to a person or a group
To compare two people or two things

to build
built

questions.q: What do the endings -ous and -al do when they are added to a word?

questions.topic: The function of the suffixes -ous and -al
questions.lesson: Forming adjectives | تكوين الصفات بإضافة ous و al
questions.why: The lesson states that -ous and -al are used to change some nouns into adjectives, e.g. fame becomes famous.

adventuring
adventurously

questions.why: nation is a noun, and adding -al gives the adjective national that describes the holiday.

questions.q: Which statement about -ous and -al is correct according to the lesson?

-ous is added to verbs and -al is added to other adjectives.
questions.topic: No fixed rule for -ous and -al: words must be memorised
questions.lesson: Forming adjectives | تكوين الصفات بإضافة ous و al
questions.why: The lesson says there is no fixed rule to know which word takes -ous and which takes -al, so they must be learnt.

questions.q: Why is the adjective from *fame* written *famous* and not *fameous*?

Because the final -e is kept only in British English
Because the final -e of the noun is dropped before -ous

questions.lesson: Forming adjectives | تكوين الصفات بإضافة ous و al

curiosity
problem

questions.topic: The final y changes to i before -ous
questions.lesson: Forming adjectives | تكوين الصفات بإضافة ous و al
questions.why: The final y of the noun changes to i before -ous, so mystery gives mysterious.

anxious
anxiousness
